question.text: An Indian importer needs to buy EUR to pay for machinery. In the OTC market, the bank quotes EUR/USD at 1.0850/1.0875 and USD/INR at 83.40/83.42. What rate will the importer pay per EUR?

explanation.text: The Logic: The importer is buying EUR, so the bank is selling EUR and the importer pays the offer side on both legs. Per pages 29-30, EUR/INR offer = EUR/USD offer x USD/INR offer = 1.0875 x 83.42 = 90.71925, which rounds to approximately 90.72. The Trap: Using the bid side on either leg would give the rate at which the bank buys EUR, not the rate at which the importer must pay. Note: Page 22 confirms that bid/offer are quoted from the bank's perspective, so customer-side direction determines which side of each quote to apply.
